programme.title: Reputations
programme.desc: Intimate portrait of Sir John Betjeman, the UK's poet laureate from 1972 until his death in 1984 and one of the most popular English poets of the 20th century. Betjeman's life was full of contrasts. He entertained the world with his warmth and enthusiasm, but, inwardly, he was haunted by fear, religious doubt, remorse and guilt. Highlighting his achievements as a conservationist and broadcaster, the film features contributions from the Prince of Wales and Lord Snowdon.

programme.title: Archaeology: A Secret History
programme.desc: Archaeologist Richard Miles presents a series charting the history of the breakthroughs and watersheds in our long quest to understand our ancient past. He begins by going back 2,000 years to explore how archaeology began by trying to prove a biblical truth - a quest that soon got archaeologists into dangerous waters.

programme.title: How the Celts Saved Britain
programme.desc: Dan Snow blows the lid off the traditional, Anglo-centric view of history and reveals how the Irish saved Britain from cultural oblivion during the Dark Ages, in this provocative, two-part documentary. Travelling back in time to some of the remotest corners of the British Isles, Dan unravels the mystery of the lost years of 400-800 AD, when the collapse of the Roman Empire left Britain in tatters. In the first episode, Dan shows how in the 5th century AD Roman 'Britannia' was plunged into chaos by the arrival of Anglo-Saxon invaders. As Roman civilisation disappeared from Britain, a new civilisation emerged in one of the most unlikely places - Ireland. Within a few generations, Christianity transformed a backward, barbarian country into the cultural powerhouse of early medieval Europe. This is a visually and intellectually stimulating journey through one of the least known chapters of British history.

programme.title: Britain in Focus: A Photographic History
programme.desc: Eamonn McCabe explores how British photographers responded to historic events in the first half of the 20th century and traces the emergence of photojournalism.

programme.title: The Secret Genius of Plants
programme.desc: Technical developments are enabling us to see the world of plants in ever greater detail, giving us insights into their remarkable abilities to adapt and survive.

programme.title: Do We Really Need the Moon?
programme.desc: The moon is such a familiar presence in the sky that most of us take it for granted. But what if it wasn't where it is now? How would that affect life on Earth? Space scientist and lunar fanatic Dr Maggie Aderin-Pocock explores our intimate relationship with the moon. Besides orchestrating the tides, the moon dictates the length of a day, the rhythm of the seasons and the very stability of our planet. Yet the moon is always on the move. In the past, it was closer to the Earth and in the future it will be farther away. That it is now perfectly placed to sustain life is pure luck, a cosmic coincidence. Using computer graphics to summon up great tides and set the Earth spinning on its side, Aderin-Pocock implores us to look at the moon afresh: to see it not as an inert rock, but as a key player in the story of our planet, past, present and future.

programme.title: Villages by the Sea
programme.desc: Ben Robinson discovers the impressive lime kilns in Solva, Wales. This picturesque 19th-century port is famous for producing quicklime, a vital ingredient in both agriculture and the building industry. The kilns here are well preserved and contributed to making the soil in farmers’ fields more alkaline, which helped to increase crop yield at a time when the nation’s population was growing. It's a pretty spot now, but Ben learns how this industry would have made life tough for the locals.

programme.title: Canal Boat Diaries
programme.desc: Autumnal fog and an overheating engine prove to be problems for narrowboater Robbie Cumming as he navigates a Roman waterway and the fast-flowing River Trent. It’s a journey of many challenges as he runs aground and breaks down in Nottingham.

programme.title: Rome: A History of the Eternal City
programme.desc: Simon Sebag Montefiore charts the rocky course of Rome's rise to become the capital of western Christendom and its impact on the lives of its citizens, elites and high priests. Rome casts aside its pantheon of pagan gods and a radical new religion takes hold. Christianity was just a persecuted sect until Emperor Constantine took a huge leap of faith, promoting it as the religion of Empire. But would this divine gamble pay off?

programme.title: Mary Beard's Ultimate Rome: Empire without Limit
programme.desc: In the fourth and final episode, Mary tackles the biggest puzzle of all: why, and how, did the Roman Empire fall? Surveying the massive walls and fortifications of Britain and Germany, she discovers an empire under pressure, struggling to control its borders. Mary seeks to redefine our understanding of the so-called 'Barbarian Invasions', but also shows that the Roman Empire was facing even greater challenges from within. Maverick emperors upset all the assumptions of right-thinking Romans, while the traditional religion and beliefs of the Roman state came head to head with the absolute conviction of Jews and Christians. Ultimately, Mary asks whether the Roman Empire was transformed rather than destroyed, and indeed lives on in the world we still see all around us - in our institutions and infrastructure, in the aspirations, methodology and symbolism of many empires since.

programme.title: I, Claudius
programme.desc: Caligula's erratic behaviour continues as he makes his horse a senator and turns the palace into a brothel. Many in the Praetorian Guard come to realise that their ruler is insane. Fearing the collapse of Rome itself, they begin to believe that something needs to be done.

programme.title: I, Claudius
programme.desc: Drama series chronicling the reigns of four Roman emperors. The mad Caligula is assassinated, and Claudius is proclaimed emperor by the Praetorian Guard.

programme.title: The Australian Wars
programme.desc: Film-maker Rachel Perkins examines what happened when the increasing number of arriving European colonists encroached upon the prime hunting grounds of Tasmanian Indigenous people.

programme.title: Villages by the Sea
programme.desc: Ben Robinson heads to Beer, Devon, home to beer stone, which has been quarried since Roman times and used in many of the nation's cathedrals and landmark buildings, including Westminster Abbey, the Tower of London and St Paul’s Cathedral. Ben finds ancient Roman arches in the quarry and discovers the stone’s origin in the village’s unique white cliffs. He also learns of the village’s lace industry and finds original lace-making needles in a house where Queen Victoria’s wedding dress lace is likely to have been made.

programme.title: Canal Boat Diaries
programme.desc: On the last leg of his 300-mile journey across the north of England and the Midlands, Robbie Cumming faces issues with ice on the Grand Union Canal, takes on Foxton’s famous lock flight in Leicestershire, and completes his journey in the picturesque village Braunston, Northamptonshire, regarded as the spiritual home for narrowboaters.

programme.title: Vasa: The Ghost Ship
programme.desc: The Vasa, one of the most majestic galleons ever to put to sea, sank 18 minutes after leaving Stockholm harbour on her maiden voyage in 1628. The loss of the Vasa was a major setback for Sweden’s ambitions to become a power in the Baltic during a turbulent period of European history. Three centuries later, in 1961, the wreck of the Vasa was raised. Remarkably well preserved by the mud and water in the Baltic Sea, she is a 17th-century time machine. Following the work of archaeologists, divers and historians, this programme plunges into Stockholm harbour to make new discoveries and reveal more about the lives of those who built, sailed and died on one of the most powerfully armed warships of her time.

programme.title: Jaws
programme.desc: When a great white shark begins preying on humans off the beaches of New England, a police chief, a shark expert and a grizzled fisherman head out on a perilous journey to hunt the creature down.

programme.title: Talking Pictures
programme.desc: Celia Imrie dives into the BBC’s archives to tell the behind-the-scenes story of Steven Spielberg’s classic aquatic horror, Jaws. It had arrived in cinemas with the warning slogan 'Don’t go in the water', but the team from the BBC’s Film 74 had already got in early, capturing the first days of shooting and filming revealing interviews with the young director, his cast and crew. These gems are combined with later archive moments that explore the entire Jaws phenomenon and its many sequels to produce a Talking Pictures that comes with extra bite.

programme.title: Jaws 2
programme.desc: Just when they thought it was safe to go back in the water, the beach-goers of Amity are threatened again by a giant, man-eating shark. Police chief Brody must convince the town of the danger and kill the shark.

programme.title: Talking Business
programme.desc: Is the space economy the next gold rush? Elon Musk's SpaceX has sparked the public's imagination after its recent stock market debut, but what will all the money being thrown into the space industry actually achieve? The founder of leading investment firm Space Capital, Chad Anderson, explains how what happens in orbit is increasingly important to the economy down on Earth. Ben Thompson also hears from the head of the UN's Office for Outer Space Affairs, Aarti Holla-Maini, about how space law is keeping up with an industry that is moving at breakneck speed. Also on the programme, the billionaire founder of New Zealand-based Rocket Lab, Sir Peter Beck, shines a light on what the private sector can achieve in space and whether SpaceX are friends or rivals.

programme.title: The Media Show
programme.desc: The death of Cambridge academic Jason Arday has prompted intense debate about media conduct, following weeks of reporting on allegations of plagiarism and questions about aspects of his life story. Critics have accused journalists of contributing to an atmosphere of relentless scrutiny, while others argue that legitimate public interest questions were being pursued. Nick Clark, a childhood friend of Jason Arday, reflects on his experience of speaking to reporters. Charles Moore, columnist at The Telegraph and The Spectator, Seun Matiluko, freelance journalist, Sarah Ditum, Times Columnist and Stephen Bush, columnist at the Financial Times, consider questions of proportionality, public interest and journalistic responsibility.

programme.title: The Trouble with KanYe
programme.desc: In October 2022, Ye, formerly known as Kanye West, drew widespread condemnation after wearing a White Lives Matter T-shirt at his Paris Fashion Show. That controversy was swiftly followed up with a series of antisemitic statements on social media. With his dangerous statements making global headlines, Ye doubled down by sharing dangerous and inflammatory mistruths during a series of interviews. In the face of backlash, Ye told the paparazzi that he was planning to run for president of the United States in 2024. Unfolding against the backdrop of Ye’s recent behaviour and his rumoured 2024 presidential campaign, this documentary sees award-winning journalist Mobeen Azhar travel to the United States to try and discover how one of America’s most celebrated artists became a megaphone for hate and division.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve is on his home turf, scouring land, sea and air for some of the deadliest critters that the UK has to offer. First, he heads for the seas off the coast of Plymouth in search of monsters from the deep. And he's not disappointed! In the bowels of a wreck he comes face to face with a giant conger eel, one of the most feared predators in the ocean. Back on land he meets a double deadly killer, the dragonfly. As adults they are amazing aerial assassins, but they lead a double life. Before they emerge as elegant winged beauties, the larvae are terrors of the underwater world, impaling their unsuspecting prey with their alien-like double-hinged jaws. Finally, with the aid of a giant vertical wind tunnel, Steve tries to hover like a kestrel, one of the prettiest but fiercest falcons.

programme.title: Jared Leto: Hollywood's Dark Secret
programme.desc: A BBC documentary has uncovered allegations of criminal sexual conduct by multiple women at the hands of Oscar-winning actor and Thirty Seconds to Mars frontman Jared Leto. All were teenagers at the time of the alleged offences. One said she was subjected to sexual assault, another that the Hollywood star threatened her with sexual assault, and a third said he had sex with her in California when she was underage, which would be classified as statutory rape. Leto won the 2014 Academy Award for best supporting actor for Dallas Buyers Club and has appeared in hit films such as Fight Club, Blade Runner 2049, Suicide Squad and, most recently, Masters of the Universe. He also has an award-winning rock band, Thirty Seconds to Mars. The film contains allegations from five other women, four of them between 16 and 18 at the time, that the star abused his celebrity status to get their phone numbers. Many of his repeated phone calls to them were sexually explicit in nature, they said.

programme.desc: Steve Backshall and his long-suffering crew return for more deadly encounters with animals hoping to earn a place on his hallowed Deadly 60 list. Out at sea, he uses radar technology to track down massive humpback whales, with a unique hunting strategy. Finally, it's back to dry land, where Steve and the crew go in search of incredible, imposing grizzly bears and witness these huge mammals in full-on deadly mode.

programme.desc: Finding himself lost and alone at Paddington station, a young Peruvian bear is befriended by the Brown family. They offer him a temporary haven while he attempts to find the explorer whose visit to Peru many years previously has taught him all he knows about the English.

programme.title: Top Gear
programme.desc: Motoring magazine. The presenters compete in an epic race across London: Jeremy in a speedboat, James in a car, Richard on his push bike and the Stig on public transport. Richard races the new Aston Martin V8 Vantage convertible against a jet-powered rollerskater and Jeremy track-tests the incredibly fast Caparo T1 road racer. The star in a reasonably priced car is Simon Cowell.

programme.title: The Young Offenders
programme.desc: Irresponsible friends Conor and Jock are up to their old tricks again, this time trying to outsmart the police by doing the exact opposite of what they would expect – with hilariously disastrous consequences. Meanwhile, pregnant Siobhán, her sister Linda and their parents Barry and Orla Walsh are all in a hospital waiting room. Today is the day of the first baby scan. Principal Walsh and Orla have had enough of Conor and Jock's irresponsible behaviour, so they come up with a plan – they’ll adopt Siobhán’s baby. The suggestion doesn’t go down well with anyone, so to bring the matter to a head and test Jock’s ability to look after a child, Principal Walsh challenges Jock to take care of an egg for a full month, without losing or breaking it. If he succeeds, Jock and Siobhán will raise the baby. If he fails, the Walshes will adopt the baby.

programme.title: The Young Offenders
programme.desc: With the baby due soon, Conor and Jock celebrate the anniversary of them officially becoming best friends. After all, best friends only come around once in a lifetime, right? Enter Gavin Madigan, a new pupil in the school, whose childhood history with Jock ignites a jealous rage in Conor. Gavin and Jock were best friends in primary school, and Gavin and his mother – Nancy, a new teacher at the school – have just moved back to Cork from Kilkenny. Conor takes an instant dislike to Gavin, who has started to intentionally call Conor the wrong name and also takes to complimenting Linda, knowing it will enrage Conor. Meanwhile, a spate of thefts at the school has Principal Walsh doubling down on his activities, patrolling the school grounds to monitor any potential thefts. When Nancy realises that an item has been stolen from her, Principal Walsh puts the school on lockdown until the culprit has been found. And Healy has taken to showing up at Mairéad’s place of work, the fish stall, to interrupt her day with some unwanted public displays of affection.

programme.title: The Young Offenders
programme.desc: A day trip in memory of Conor's dad and the appearance of some mysterious cash cause confusion, with the interference of Billy Murphy creating a perfect storm of mayhem.

programme.title: The Young Offenders
programme.desc: Billy Murphy enlists the help of Conor, Jock and eventually Mairead to avoid getting killed by a former cellmate who has just been released from prison.

programme.desc: Jane Nicholas has been a bridesmaid at 27 weddings and is happy to work at a Manhattan magazine run by entrepreneur George, on whom she has an unrequited crush. When her younger sister Tess arrives back from Europe after a whirlwind romance, Jane is inevitably asked to be Tess's bridesmaid. Jane's happy routine is punctuated by Kevin, a cynical journalist who writes the 'commitments' column for a New York magazine.

programme.title: Angels of the North
programme.desc: The Angels of the North are back, and Sammyjo has a busy weekend of christening celebrations ahead; she is godmother to not one, but two goddaughters. First up it’s an all Longlox affair, as Sammyjo takes on the party planning for the christening of stylist Kendal’s daughter Kyra. Pure Ink piercer Jade is throwing the second christening of the weekend for her newborn, Alayah, leaving brother Shane to search for his first ever suit and wrestle with having to buy shoes – another first. With the Longlox girls and Pure Ink crew coming together for the happy occasions, Sammyjo is surrounded by her work family and her real family.

programme.title: Angels of the North
programme.desc: Sammyjo is looking for love and taking the plunge into the world of dating apps. Will swiping left and right unlock the secret to finding a new man? Or will afternoon tea and some words of wisdom from Grandma Eileen help her find Mr Right? In the salon, someone is hiding a secret, a pregnancy test is missing from the kitchen, but who is expecting? The Longlox girls are left guessing while getting glammed up for a night at the races. Will a flutter on the horses see the girls past the winning post? At Pure Ink, Jade is back at work and keen to earn, but she needs help with childcare. Can ‘Uncle Shane’ get over his fear of nappies and take on the babysitting?

programme.title: Angels of the North
programme.desc: The funfair ‘The Hoppins’ arrives in the toon. While Shane conquers a newfound fear of heights on ‘the bomber’, Sammyjo and the girls are running for cover as ‘the curse of the Hoppins’ strikes. Pure Ink piercer Carla is back from a festival, and after a mix-up in the mosh pit, she is carrying an injury and wants anyone and everyone to hear her story. Sammyjo turns to friend Frankie for dating advice ahead of a singles night out, while at the salon, there is an unexpected staffroom surprise as we find out who is pregnant.

programme.title: Bergerac
programme.desc: The race is on to find Kim before she comes to harm. But just as Barney and Kara are making progress, Bergerac gets a chilling phone call. Will he be able to save Kim? Meanwhile, Arthur is getting his house in order, but as Barney prepares to question Margaret one more time, Bergerac has a shocking realisation about the case.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: A poster collection tops the bill in this episode from West Sussex. In Horsham, Charlie Ross marvels at historic posters collected by local man William Albery. Examples include an appeal for a stolen fat sheep, a concert to raise money for the victims of the Titanic and instructions on how to avoid catching Spanish flu. Each poster demonstrates the bold typography and social history that Albery loved so much. Hoping to post the biggest profit at auction is the red team, friends Kully and Arti, who reckon that the blues are going to lose. Their opponents are mum and daughter Judith and Tilly who are in it to win it. Among the stalls of Ardingly antiques fair, Kully spots colourful signs painted on scaffold boards, including one about kite flying – until expert Jonathan Pratt decides it may crash at auction. Inside, Judith spies a silver bookmark in the shape of a trowel. She’s thinking constructively – but expert Kate Bliss isn’t impressed by its lack of age. In Buckinghamshire, auctioneer Hugo Lemon works hard for the teams, but what can JP rustle up for his bonus buy – with only one pound to spend?

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: Jacqui Joseph is at Altrincham Recycling Centre in Greater Manchester with an eagle eye, hoping to swoop in on quality items before they are lost forever. A mysterious wooden post leaves lighting designer Duncan scratching his head, and Jacqui tries to get a dated rocking chair back in full swing. Will she manage to send all three items off to new homes?

programme.title: The Great British Sewing Bee
programme.desc: It's Children’s Week. In the Pattern Challenge, the sewers tackle a children’s tutu. In the Transformation Challenge, sustainability is key as the sewers repurpose fleece into stuffed animal toys with adorable results. Finally, mini models are welcomed into the sewing room for the Made-to-Measure Challenge. The sewers are tasked with creating an outfit for their very own superhero creations. Who will handle it like child’s play, and who will be sent to the naughty step?

Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted by the House of Games reusable coffee mug, which is brand new for this series?

programme.title: The Edge
programme.desc: Gabby Logan takes charge of the quiz where contestants need brainpower and ball skills to win big. Who will be the high roller and who will push themselves over The Edge?

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: Comedian and presenter Susan Calman, internet star Max Fosh and DJ Noreen Khan are back as the week moves on to its second stop. Vernon Kay keeps the quiz on track, while Traitors star Paul Gorton is back as an unreliable tour guide, turning the spotlight on Enniskillen and its surprising stories. With scores beginning to take shape, attention shifts towards who could become the week's overall champion.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: The lives of the park’s rock hyrax babies hang in the balance as their mum is taken to the vets for an urgent medical investigation. The keepers have spotted worrying lumps on the mum, Dozy, which might be affecting how her youngsters feed from her. With Dozy at the vets, the babies are alone, so it’s a race against time to do the investigation and get mum back to her babies before they get too hungry. Elsewhere, there are some arrivals in the park who have been missing since the mid-nineteenth century – red squirrels. Their numbers have dwindled as they face competition from the non-native grey squirrels that are destroying the natural parkland. The keepers are embarking on a red squirrel breeding programme to help save these beautiful animals from extinction in the UK, but they need to create an enclosure that encourages the squirrels to mate. Meanwhile, Kate helps keep the cheetah in peak physical condition with some high-intensity training, Ben creates a mud bath for the European wolves, and out on safari Jean Johansson learns how to recognise individual zebras and tests the eyesight of an ostrich.

programme.title: Serengeti
programme.desc: All our animal families make the most of the good times when a new oasis brings untold riches. But they face devastation when a towering inferno takes over. Will anyone survive?

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: A set of musical drinking glasses, a pianists finger stretcher and Harry Lauder's piano give this edition from Dumfries a musical flavour. But Michael Aspel and the experts also find rare local silver, a valuable doll and a collection of drawings by Beatrix Potter worth a small fortune.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin presents from the Watts Gallery in Surrey, a treasure trove of British art and sculpture. The experts Thomas Plant and David Harper are on hand to find a selection of objects to take to auction. Thomas values an art deco flapper girl, while a trio of pocket watches impresses David. Paul also visits the heathland known as the Devil's Punchbowl to uncover gruesome tales of highway robbery.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, former winners Jimi Famurewa, Harriet Kemsley, Colin Murray and Sara Pascoe take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall House of Champions winner being crowned on Friday. Will they opt for the House of Games golden cowboy hat, or instead go for the must-have golden wheelie luggage?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway journey reaches the naval port of Brest, home to France’s oceanographic fleet. Aboard the pride of the fleet, the 107-metre-long Pourquoi Pas, Michael hears how marine biologists deploy research submersibles 6,000 metres below the surface to study life in the deep sea. In the kitchen of a traditional boulangerie, Michael learns how to make a Breton favourite, a sweet, buttery cake called kouign-amann. The taste for Breton culture leads him to Guingamp, where he attempts to keep up with a Breton dance troupe rehearsing for the regional dance championships. On the windswept north coast, with some of the highest tides in the world, Michael visits Brittany’s largest nature reserve, which attracts over 100 bird species.

programme.title: Nigellissima
programme.desc: Nigella shares her culinary talent as she presents delicious Italian-inspired food. In this episode, Nigella reveals a secret passion for one of the tastes of Italy with her dark and deviant liquorice pudding, before introducing us to the joys of fregola - the Sardinian sun-dried and toasted couscous - in a light, tomato-hued recipe of couscous with clams. Nigella's dinner party guests are served a simple yet sumptuous meal of butterflied leg of lamb and baby aubergines with oregano and roasted red onion. Dessert is an irresistible meringue gelato cake with sharp raspberries and a dark chocolate sauce.

programme.title: Race Against the Tide
programme.desc: Six teams return to St Andrews Beach for a deeply personal challenge: sculpting what home means to them in just six hours, before the tide sweeps in. From Welsh valleys and family legacies to artistic studios and symbols of rebirth, creativity meets chaos as collapses and comebacks keep the pressure high. Judges Sadie and Jamie expect emotional depth and technical brilliance but don’t anticipate the surprise twist of an ending - so who will rise and who will crumble under the weight of the ever-looming waves?

programme.title: Saving Lives at Sea
programme.desc: When a mayday comes in from a yacht breaking up on a sandbank off the Norfolk coast, both the Great Yarmouth and Gorleston RNLI crew and two of Caister’s independent lifeboats race to the rescue. In Pembrokeshire, the St Davids crew are alerted to two paddleboarders in distress, but their location is eight miles away - and it will take at least half an hour to reach them. Just off the coast of Scarborough, a fisherman has slipped on rocks and has a suspected broken ankle; in fading light and a rising tide, the crew face a tricky extraction. And across the Irish Sea, in Skerries, there are reports of two swimmers in difficulty near Shenick Island.

programme.title: Emergency 24/7
programme.desc: Two trauma calls reveal that the greatest dangers are not always the most obvious, testing the expertise, judgement and resilience of the emergency team at Southmead Hospital. They battle to save Paul, whose leg has been severed after being hit by a train but who is in more immediate danger from an overdose that could cause severe liver damage. And they question the story of a man with a deep wound who denies being stabbed.

programme.title: Live at the Apollo
programme.desc: Maisie Adam introduces comedians Michael Odewale and Susie McCabe to the stage.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Adam Fleming.

programme.title: Interview with the Vampire
programme.desc: Armand’s demands test Louis to his limits, Lestat’s soul-searching revives memories, and Daniel’s bowling is disrupted.

programme.title: A House Through Time
programme.desc: In the Victorian era, the residents of the house on Calton Hill include Thomas Mains, a maker of expensive shoes whose customers won’t pay. His wife, Ann, eventually takes the customers to court after his death. There's also Thomas Glen, a world-famous bagpipe maker who runs a musical instrument shop in the city, early photographer Archibald Burns, and a notorious brothel keeper, the mysterious Catherine Johnston.

programme.title: Celebrity MasterChef
programme.desc: It’s the first of the heats, and this week, the five celebrities up for the culinary challenge are Joe Pasquale, Jason Mohammad, Emily Campbell, Shakira Khan and Jay McGuiness.

programme.title: Captive Audience: A Real American Horror Story
programme.desc: A heroic escape. A televised family reunion. But the Stayner ordeal is far from over. When a hit TV movie rewrites the Stayner story, reality gets stranger than fiction.

programme.desc: Nicki Chapman helps Jules and Sharlean leave the edge of Chester behind in search of Cheshire’s rural charms and undiscovered dog walks. The house search throws up some tempting contenders, including a mystery house that’s a little cheeky about its postcode. Elsewhere, Nicki meets a retired professional rugby player and his wife, who have brewed up a successful new life running a specialty coffee shop.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: In Buckinghamshire, Sarah Moore sifts through boots full of rubbish at Beaconsfield Recycling Centre in the hope of finding three gems amongst the junk. Sarah risks getting her fingers burnt creating candlesticks from old spindles, and a last-minute change of plan by Simion throws the cat among the creative pigeons.

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael boards the Eurostar at London’s St Pancras International, bound for the Belgian capital, Brussels. In the city centre’s sumptuous Theatre Royal, he learns how an impassioned opera performance led to revolution on the streets and the birth of an independent nation. Travelling by tram to the residential district of Saint Gilles, Michael discovers the Belgian origins of art nouveau at the elegant house of architect Victor Horta. Finishing his first day at the headquarters of Nato, opened in 1967, he recalls his time as defence secretary and enjoys a private viewing of its impressive archive.

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s Belgian rail journey continues in the Dutch speaking region of Flanders. In Antwerp, he discovers the city's historic multibillion-pound diamond industry and drops in at the workshop of an expert. Just outside the city, Michael boards the Dendermonde to Puurs Heritage Railway, run by volunteers, and gets a chance to drive one of its 1950s diesel engines. Heading to Belgium’s third city, Ghent, Michael visits the magnificent cathedral and marvels at a 15th-century Van Eyck masterpiece, the Adoration of the Mystic Lamb, the most stolen painting in the world.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: The keepers make an exciting discovery in the emu barn - a clutch of eggs. Could the park finally get its first emu chick? The male emu is supposed to sit on the eggs, but so far this dad hasn't got the memo. Will this year be any different? The keepers are doing everything they can to help the potential parents, but they aren’t keeping their eggs in one basket - they’ve hatched another plan. Some of the eggs have been put in incubators, and there are promising signs. Elsewhere, it’s touch-and-go again with the rock hyrax babies. Earlier in the series, the keepers were concerned about some lumps on the mum, but now they have another worry - the adult male is attacking the babies. The keepers must quickly find out why. Will harmony ever be restored to this family? Also, Kate gets the chance to observe an incredible wild visitor to the park – a white-tailed sea eagle – and Jean Johansson helps out with a moth survey.

programme.title: Serengeti
programme.desc: A great fire leaves homes destroyed and families separated. The animal characters must find new ways to survive in an unrecognisable and inhospitable landscape.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team visit Cressing Temple Barns in Essex. Amongst the rare finds are a collection of ventriloquist's dummies, an Italian chair by Bugatti, a watercolour by Russell Flint and a Chippendale table.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog it! comes from Chiddingstone Castle in Kent. Antiques experts Thomas Plant and Adam Partridge find some fascinating antiques and collectibles to take to auction. Paul Martin visits Chartwell House, home of Sir Winston Churchill, to uncover the real man behind the politician.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, former winners Jimi Famurewa, Harriet Kemsley, Colin Murray and Sara Pascoe take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s railway adventure reaches Rennes, capital of Brittany. At the Lycee Emile Zola, he hears how, in 1899, the school was used as a military court for the second trial of Alfred Dreyfus, an army captain who was twice wrongfully convicted of spying for Germany. He finds the story of racism, injustice, establishment cover-up and freedom of the press all too familiar to modern ears. Rennes’s new generation driverless metro speeds Michael across the city to the giant Stellantis car factory, where Michael joins a quality control inspection in a car that’s hot off the production line. In the historic walled citadel of St Malo, he traces the voyages of the 16th century explorer Jacques Cartier, who claimed Canada for France. Climbing the steps of Mont-Saint-Michel, Michael reflects on the layers of history evident in the abbey’s architecture and many uses over the centuries.

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Actors, lifelong friends and stars of the classic 70s mods and rockers cult movie Quadrophenia, Leslie Ash and Phil Daniels exchange their scooters for a stand-out 1950s pink Cadillac and swap the streets of Brighton for the country lanes around Lincolnshire. Joining them for the ride are antiques experts Phil Serrell and Serhat Ahmet. This iconic quartet rock'n'roll their way through the local antique shops, before finding out about Lincolnshire's star-studded history as home to the world's first music festival. Both Leslie and Phil are self-proclaimed lovers of vintage, so whose pre-existing knowledge, as well as expert guidance, will help them be victorious at auction?

programme.title: Inside the Factory
programme.desc: New presenter Paddy McGuinness makes a nostalgic visit to the Warburtons bread factory in his hometown of Bolton, where he had a Saturday job more than 30 years ago.

programme.title: 9/11: Inside the President's War Room
programme.desc: Twelve hours with the president on 9/11 – with direct testimony from President Bush, Vice-President Cheney and senior staff – as it changed them, America and the world.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Paddy O'Connell.

programme.title: Couples Therapy
programme.desc: Shay and Clinton are set homework to learn to compromise. Marjorie uncovers deep-rooted shame and trauma that shed light on her difficulties with Jason, and Drea pushes for change in her relationship with Nessa.

programme.title: Couples Therapy
programme.desc: Sienna explores how childhood bullying led her to bury uncomfortable feelings. Shay reckons with the lasting impact of her domineering mother. Nessa and Drea take a surprising turn, and Jason’s anger exposes old wounds he’s projecting onto his son.

programme.title: Buried with Michael Sheen
programme.desc: Ten years after a dying whistleblower's warning, Michael Sheen follows a trail of toxic chemical dumping in Wales and asks whether it could still be harming people’s health. His search leads him to Ruabon in north Wales, where many locals have voiced concerns about what they believe is a high incidence of cancer in the community. He also gets himself tested for PCB contamination in his own blood and brings together affected communities, scientists, environmentalists and politicians at the Welsh Parliament. Search BBC Sounds to listen to the podcast Buried: The Last Witness, which the series is based on.

programme.title: Celebrity MasterChef
programme.desc: The week’s heats continue in full swing, with the five celebrities facing two more culinary challenges as they battle for a place in this week's quarter-final. First up is the return of the mystery box challenge in which the celebrities find an ingredient, and they have just one hour to invent and cook a dish with it. They must use all their imagination, knowledge and skill to create something special. Then, for the first time in their heat, they have to cook to stay in the competition, and won’t just be trying to impress Grace and Giorgio. This crucial round is called Who’s Coming to Dinner?, with a special guest setting a culinary brief for the contestants. This week sees Paddy McGuinness enter the MasterChef kitchen, and he’s looking for the ultimate pie. But what will win him over? Classic and traditional, or something with a twist? Everything will need to be on point, as at the end of this task, one celebrity will be the first to head home. The four remaining will be counting their lucky stars as they head into this year’s first quarter-final and become one step closer to their dream of being crowned Celebrity MasterChef Champion 2026.

programme.title: Brexit: A Very British Civil War
programme.desc: As David Cameron wins a shock majority at the 2015 general election, the implications immediately dawn on all concerned. There is no coalition negotiation to stop the Conservatives from fulfilling an election pledge to hold a referendum on whether Britain should leave the EU. Nigel Farage fails to win a seat and resigns as UKIP leader but quickly U-turns. He sets up Leave.EU to campaign for Brexit. Meanwhile, as Cameron continues his negotiation with the EU, his demands are watered down. It makes it even more important he recruits Boris Johnson and Michael Gove to the Remain campaign - but they haven't yet made a decision.

Their search uncovers an irresistible mix of properties, from a home with breathtaking views, and another with its own turret, to a remarkable wing of a grand county mansion. Along the way, Sonali heads to Exmoor to meet a young family who left London behind three years ago to embrace a very different way of life on their 23-acre farm.

For her own project, Sarah has a light bulb moment revamping old lampshades.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: Vernon Kay hosts as the quiz rolls into Bamburgh. As ever, Paul Gorton leads the unreliable tour, mixing facts with a few well-placed fibs along the way. Comedian and presenter Susan Calman, internet star Max Fosh and DJ Noreen Khan are all keen to finish the week on a high and see who walks away with the 'I Know My Place' sweatshirt.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: It’s the tenth anniversary of the arrival of rescue elephant Anne, who spent most of her life in the circus. Kate and Ben find out how one of Europe’s oldest elephants is kept in the best possible condition. The team have a finely honed routine, tending to her every need – from breakfast to dinner, showers to entertainment. Kate treats Anne to some special snacks, and Jean Johansson discovers how the team keep her trunk in shape. To discourage the lions from climbing the trees close to the perimeter fence, a large-scale building project is underway in Lion Country. The new play area for these apex predators will offer them places to climb and take refuge on rainy days. It needs to be very robust, made of huge logs and wooden platforms. The only concern is whether it will be strong enough to hold the whole pride. Ben joins the keepers as the lions explore their new installation for the very first time. Wildlife camera operator Hamza Yassin joins the tigers for lunch and witnesses some unique behaviour, and Jean Johansson lends the keepers a hand feeding the koalas.

programme.title: Serengeti
programme.desc: The land recovers, and the action now centres around the river. Kali, the lioness, loses her cubs when they accidentally stray into the path of Nalla and the elephant herd. Separated from their mother, the cubs are in peril. Will Kali find them before it's too late? Nearby, we meet an adorable baby hippo, Mafuta, as he learns to survive in his riverine home. Just staying afloat is a challenge for this newborn, and Magamba, the crocodile, also has him in her sights. Only Mafuta’s father can save him, but confronting the fearsome Magamba won’t be easy. Duma, the young cheetah, is still struggling to find his place since he was separated from his family by the fire. Like all young males, he should be looking for a team of other males to help him hunt. Instead, he misguidedly tries to join a female and her cub. Utani, the mongoose, takes the pup he cares for to visit a herd of playful gazelles, but they turn out to be a little too playful for one so young. When the games are over, the mongoose pack is attacked by a hungry eagle. Could Tamu, the playful gazelle fawn, be their unlikely saviour?

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel's team of experts assess antiques brought for scrutiny by the public. They're excited to see an original manuscript by 19th-century adventure writer RM Ballantyne, as well as continental furniture and glass, a rare mustard spoon and a silver picnic set. Plus a trip to Chichester Cathedral.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Today’s Flog It! comes from Barrow Hill Railway Heritage Centre in Derbyshire. Hundreds of people arrive with their antiques and collectibles and today’s experts seek out some interesting items to take off to auction. Paul Martin finds out all about the history of this fascinating railway centre.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, former winners Jimi Famurewa, Harriet Kemsley, Colin Murray and Sara Pascoe take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall House of Champions winner being crowned on Friday. Will they opt for the House of Games golden cowboy hat, or instead go for the must-have golden wheelie luggage?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: At the medieval town of Bayeux, Michael Portillo heads for the Bayeux Tapestry Museum to admire the striking 70-metre-long work of art commissioned to record William the Conqueror’s claim to the English throne and the Battle of Hastings in 1066. On the Normandy coastline, from which William launched his invasion, Michael recalls the D-Day landings of 1944. Crossing Gold Beach in a 1943 Willys Jeep, Michael hears how the largest amphibious invasion in the history of warfare unfolded. He is moved to visit the beautifully kept Bayeux War Cemetery, where 4,600 of the dead are buried. Close to Argentan, Michael reaches the Versailles of horses, France’s 300-year-old national stud, the Haras du Pin. He tours the magnificent estate in a splendid carriage pulled by a pair of Normandy’s emblematic Percheron horses, before enjoying a taste of competitive carriage driving at the World Championships.

programme.title: Cricket: Today at the Test
programme.desc: Day 1 highlights from the second Test match between England and Pakistan at Lord's.

programme.title: The Big Deal with Steph McGovern
programme.desc: The five remaining pairs continue their mission to become art dealers in the highly competitive art world as the pressure ramps up. They explore the world of prints and limited editions in Margate, the traditional seaside town that’s been transformed into a vibrant art destination. With over 30 galleries and artist studios, as well as the Turner Contemporary Gallery, which attracts over a quarter of a million visitors a year, it’s the perfect place to test the dealers’ ability to sell directly to the public. Steph and series mentor Cordelia de Freitas are joined by artist and Margate gallery owner, Margo McDaid - someone who knows the value of the local print and limited-edition market.

programme.title: A House Through Time
programme.desc: During the first two decades of the 20th century, life for many in Edinburgh is hard. The demolition of the slums in the Old Town has put pressure on living spaces, and the house on Calton Hill has been subdivided to accommodate more families. Featured are the Marshalls, a family of five occupying just two rooms and sharing the floor and toilet with another household; the Ross family, including head prison warder James, who is brutally attacked by an inmate; and Annie Anthony and her son John, a professional soldier who fought a very different sort of war.
